summary: Halyard template mutual NDA with Skandia Logistik AB edits that add a one-way Halyard non-compete, delete two carve-outs, and move law and jurisdiction to Sweden, plus a request to cut survival.

findings.quote: Halyard shall not provide software or services similar to those discussed under the Purpose to any other logistics or freight transport enterprise operating in the Nordic region
findings.why: The inserted wording restricts only Halyard from dealing with other Nordic logistics customers during the term and for 12 months after, which is a non-compete/exclusivity restriction.
findings.draft_redline: 2.1.2 not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept a restriction on Halyard's business dealings in an NDA, as the agreement is intended only to protect confidential information. We have restored the original wording.

findings.quote: is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
findings.why: The carve-out for information lawfully received from a third party has been deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
findings.note_to_counterparty: The third-party-source exception is a standard protection for both parties, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: The independent development carve-out has been deleted, so another of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The independent-development exception is a standard mutual protection, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: The obligations set out in Clause 2 shall not apply to any information which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records
findings.why: Deleting 'or other reasonable evidence' leaves a 'written records' evidence standard, which the playbook allows.

findings.quote: the substantive law of [[DEL: England and Wales]] [[INS: Sweden]]
findings.why: Governing law is changed from England and Wales to Sweden, which is not an acceptable position.
findings.draft_redline: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the substantive law of England and Wales.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to agree Swedish governing law. We can offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts if that helps.

findings.quote: [[INS: District Court of Stockholm (Stockholms tingsrätt)]] shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: Exclusive jurisdiction is moved from the courts of England and Wales to the Stockholm District Court, outside England and Wales.
findings.draft_redline: Each Party irrevocably agrees that the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with this Agreement or its subject matter or formation.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to agree exclusive jurisdiction in Stockholm. We can offer non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

findings.quote: Can we reduce the 3-year period to 2 years and remove the open-ended Trade Secret survival tail?
findings.why: The comment asks for 2-year survival, which is acceptable, but also removal of Trade Secret protection, which the request rule says must be kept, so the request cannot be accepted as made.
findings.draft_redline: 10.3 The obligations of confidentiality and non-use contained in this Agreement shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of two (2) years from the effective date of expiry or termination, save that in respect of any Confidential Information that constitutes a Trade Secret, such obligations shall continue in full force and effect for so long as that information remains a Trade Secret under applicable law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We can agree to reduce the survival period to two years. We need to keep protection for Trade Secrets for as long as they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: shall continue in full force and effect for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: [[DEL: ten]] [[INS: twenty]] Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Return or destruction period lengthened to twenty Business Days, which is above the 5 Business Day minimum; backup and legal retention exceptions remain in clause 6.2.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: copies of any Confidential Information that are securely stored in routine, automated electronic backup or archiving systems
findings.why: Retention of automated backups and legally required copies is permitted and they stay confidential under clause 6.3.

findings.quote: which is disclosed by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party in connection with the Purpose
findings.why: The definition covers information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential, includes derived notes and analyses, and applies to either party.

findings.quote: Disclosing Party means the Party that discloses, or procures the disclosure of, Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined so either party can be either, and the obligations bind both equally.

findings.quote: regarding a potential commercial relationship between them [[INS: concerning supply chain and freight management software]]
findings.why: The Purpose is the preferred commercial-relationship wording narrowed to a named subject area, and use is limited solely to the Purpose in clause 2.1.2.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group members on a need-to-know basis with full liability for them matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice is qualified by legal permission, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, and all intellectual property rights in or relating to it, shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted beyond use for the Purpose under 7.2.

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation or gives any warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy, completeness, adequacy or fitness for a particular purpose of any Confidential Information
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty, fraud is carved out of the exclusion in 7.4, and 7.5 gives no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: The Parties do not anticipate that the disclosure of Confidential Information for the Purpose will involve the sharing or processing of any personal data
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any other sharing needs a separate DPA first; the EU GDPR addition to the definition is consistent with this.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief with cumulative remedies in 11.2.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: No assignment by either party without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: in England [[INS: or Sweden]] when banks in London [[INS: and Stockholm]] are open for business
findings.why: The Business Day definition adds Swedish holidays and Stockholm banks, which is a customary drafting change that affects only how time periods are counted.
findings.fallback_cited: Any customary drafting, including archaic wording of standard positions.
